name: Bitwarden
description: A cloud-synced password manager with apps and browser extensions everywhere. Vaults are encrypted on your device before they sync. Use Bitwarden's own cloud or host the server yourself.
licenseNote: Clients are GPL-3.0 and the server is AGPL-3.0, with some enterprise server modules under the source-available Bitwarden License. Premium and organisation features need a paid plan even when you self-host.
backing: Bitwarden, Inc. (US, venture-backed), funded by subscriptions

maturity.rationale: Millions of users, published third-party security audits every year and a long, stable track record.

selfHosting.summary: The standard deployment is a multi-container stack built around Microsoft SQL Server. For households and home labs, the official 'lite' deployment is a single container that works with SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL. Most people simply use Bitwarden's cloud, where the free plan is enough for one person.

requirements.notes: For the standard deployment. The single-container lite deployment runs in a few hundred megabytes.

managedHosting.label: Bitwarden Cloud
managedHosting.note: Free for individuals; paid family and business plans, with US or EU data regions

strengths: Polished apps and browser extensions on every platform
Imports directly from 1Password, LastPass, Dashlane and dozens more
A free hosted plan with unlimited passwords and devices
Regular third-party security audits, published in full
weaknesses: Some features cost money wherever you host: integrated one-time codes, emergency access, advanced reports
Autofill is a little less smooth than 1Password's
The full self-hosted stack is heavy and built around SQL Server
Enterprise server modules are source-available rather than open source

featureNotes.team-sharing: Organisations; the free tier covers two people
featureNotes.totp: A Premium feature; a separate free authenticator app exists
featureNotes.offline-vault: Encrypted exports, but the live vault syncs through a server
